title: The Duplicate Dilemma
subtitle: Something in the library records doesn't add up
conceptSummary: When filtering TEXT values, always use single quotes: WHERE city = 'Mumbai' (not Mumbai).

dialogue.text: I tried to look up premium members from Bangalore. My query failed. Help!
You forgot the quotes around the text value. SQL needs quotes for text. Every. Single. Time.
Can you fix my broken query? It should find all premium members.

teachMoment.title: Text Values Need Quotes!
teachMoment.body:
When your WHERE condition involves TEXT, wrap the value in single quotes:

✅ WHERE membership_type = 'premium'
❌ WHERE membership_type = premium

Without quotes, SQL thinks 'premium' is a column name — and panics.

task.instruction: Fix Byte's broken query. It should return all 'premium' members.
task.brokenQuery:
SELECT name, city, membership_type
FROM members
WHERE membership_type = premium
task.solution: SELECT name, city, membership_type FROM members WHERE membership_type = 'premium'

hints.text: Look at the WHERE clause. Something is missing around the word premium.
Text values need quotes! Try: WHERE membership_type = 'premium'
Full fix: SELECT name, city, membership_type FROM members WHERE membership_type = 'premium'

winDialogue.text: 4 premium members. And one of them — Kavya Rao — has borrowed 3 books at once. That's the maximum!
Nothing suspicious about that. But cross-check with the pizza orders. Is Kavya connected to SHADOW42?

storyBeat: Kavya Rao — a premium library member from Bangalore — is also a regular at Pizza Palace. Her name doesn't appear on SHADOW42 orders... but someone from her IP did access the database.
